mes-an-ni-pad-da: Mesannipadda (Langdon Mes-an-ni-pad-da) — first king of Ur; the first sign is DUB (Langdon: 'clearly DUP'), read mes
mes-ki-aĝ₂-{d}nanna: Meskiaĝnanna (Langdon Mes-ki-em-ᵈNannar) — king of Ur, son of Mesannipadda; mes (DUB) + ki-aĝ₂ 'love' (AĜ₂, Langdon em) + the moon-god Nanna (ŠEŠ.KI, Langdon Nannar)
e-lu-lu: Elulu — king of Ur; the name is not on this prism, restored by Langdon from other copies
ba-lu-lu: Balulu — king of Ur; the name is not on this prism, restored by Langdon from other copies
a-wa-an: Awan (Langdon A-wa-an) — a land east of Babylonia, toward Elam; written A-PI-AN + place-determinative ki, PI read wa
ku-ul-[…]: Kul… (Langdon Ku-ul (?)) — king of Awan; the second sign is damaged and its reading uncertain, the rest of the name lost
laḫ₄-[…]: Laḫ… (Langdon Laḫ (?)) — first king of the second dynasty of Kish; the first sign is damaged, taken as LAḪ₄ (DU over DU), the rest lost; reading uncertain
da-da-sig: Dadasig — king of Kish (second dynasty); DA-DA-SIG
ma₂-ma₂-gal-[…]: Mamagal… (Langdon Má-má-gal) — king of Kish (second dynasty); MA₂-MA₂-GAL, then a damaged sign and a break, so the end of the name is uncertain
ka-al-bu-um: Kalbum (Langdon Ka-al-bu-[um]) — king of Kish (second dynasty), son of Magalgal…; Semitic-looking name in -um
ma₂-gal-gal-[…]: Magalgal… (Langdon Má-gal-gal) — father of Kalbum; MA₂-GAL-GAL, then a break; perhaps the Mamagal… of an earlier line spelled differently, which is uncertain
umuš-e: Umushe (Langdon Umuš-e) — king of Kish (second dynasty); the first sign is read umuš by Langdon, its identification uncertain, + E
x-nun-na: …-nunna — king of Kish (second dynasty); the first sign is unread (Langdon '?', fn.: 'PISAN + RU ?'), so the name is incomplete; nun-na as in other royal names
i-bi-ni-iš: Ibinish (Langdon I-bi-ni-iš (?)) — king of Kish (second dynasty); an erased sign stands between bi and ni and the last sign is damaged, so the reading is uncertain
lugal-mu: Lugalmu (Langdon Lugal-mu, 'Lugalmu (?)') — last king of the second dynasty of Kish; lugal 'king' + mu (perhaps 'my'), so the sense of the name is uncertain
ḫa-ma-zi: Hamazi (Langdon Ḫa-ma-ṣi) — a city or land, seat of a dynasty of one king; ḪA-MA-ZI + place-determinative ki; Langdon's ṣi is the ZI sign, read zi by sign
ḫa-da-ni-iš: Hadanish (Langdon Ḫa-da-ni-iš) — the one king of Hamazi

__broaden__.-ma: genitive -a(k) 'of', written -ma after a final m (elam{ki}-ma 'of Elam') · locative -a 'in, at', likewise written -ma after a final m (urim₂{ki}-ma 'in Ur')
